data.gender_notes: Irita is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Irita was the goddess of the rainbow. Her name is derived from the Greek word for rainbow, 'iris'. The name Irita carries the meaning “Goddess of the Rainbow” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Irita usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the rainbow and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of unity and harmony between the physical and spiritual worlds.
data.etymology: Irita belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Rainbow.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Irita total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Irita, inspired by the Greek goddess of the rainbow, symbolizes a connection to the natural world and its beauty. It may represent a deep appreciation or reverence for the splendor and diversity of life.
data.spiritual_significance: In a Christian context, Irita can be seen as a reminder of the bridge between this world and the next. The rainbow represents the promise and covenant between God and man – until the end of days, God will not send another flood to destroy the earth. The name Irita, though rooted in a pagan mythology, can symbolize the spiritual connection between God and his people, and the promise of hope and renewal.
